in.other_title: Expected Agent Score (EAS) as a capability measure generalizing debater Elo
in.rationale: Khan et al. introduce persuasiveness, measured by judge approval without ground-truth labels, to study debate scaling. Sudhir et al. state they generalise the debater Elo used in earlier debate experiments, which they equate with persuasiveness in Khan et al., to other scalable oversight protocols with Expected Agent Score, EAS = (log p_true, log p_false) dotted with q, as a pure capability measure; only Khan et al.'s persuasiveness is stated to be label-free.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: measures of agent strength for studying how oversight protocols scale with capability

in.rationale: Like Khan et al., the authors track the relationship between debater skill and judge accuracy, and they measure skill by win rate against other training checkpoints, whereas Khan et al. measure persuasiveness by judge approval and generate a range of expert models with inference-time methods. in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: Method for testing whether an oversight protocol stays truth-seeking under optimization; applies to training checkpoints rather than inference-time variants; Khan et al.'s models are evaluated by unseen LLM judges whose preferences have not been optimized for, while the cited Arnesen et al. passage does not say whether its judge is held out

in.other_title: The authors generalize Khan et al.'s Elo persuasiveness measure into Expected Agent Score
in.rationale: Khan et al. define an Elo-based persuasiveness metric from judge approval in debate; the authors explicitly build on it and generalize it to other scalable oversight protocols by defining Expected Agent Score, EAS = (log p⊤, log p⊥) · q, as a pure measure of the agent's capabilities.
in.scope: proposed EXTENDS: How to measure agent capability when relating it to judge accuracy; applies to the authors' generalized protocol framework.
